summary: A designer's project page for a free geometric sans (Figtree), built like a polished product landing page: aerial-ocean photo hero, a weight-labelled list of editable UI-ish lines, an annotated outline 'tag!' on yellow, a variable slider tester with parallax iridescent blobs, a navy feature board whose 'after' column types itself, and design notes whose inline glyph chips load a sticky glyph inspector.

instances.look: Full-screen aerial photo of turquoise sea with a tiny sailboat; 'figtree' in white at ~200px Bold, 'A new, friendly (free!) sans serif' under it and a small dark 'GET IT ↓' button
instances.ux: Button jumps to #download; fixed 'E' logo top-left and grey DOWNLOAD button top-right stay on screen
instances.learn: A calm, wordless photo plus a three-word promise ('friendly, free') is enough for a free UI font

reconstruction.layout: 100vh full-bleed background image; content block left-aligned at x≈430, name at y≈335–525, subtitle y≈580, button y≈650; boat PNG layered separately near top-right
reconstruction.typography: Name ~200px Figtree wght 650–700, white, tight tracking; subtitle ~22px Regular white; button ~12px caps SemiBold
reconstruction.behaviour: Static (ocean image is a CSS background div; boat is a separate layer, possibly parallax)
reconstruction.assets: Aerial ocean photograph; sailboat PNG cut-out

instances.look: Weight names in tiny grey caps in a left column (MEDIUM, BLACK, REGULAR, EXTRABOLD, LIGHT, BLACK, SEMIBOLD, REGULAR) beside editable lines in dark teal: a nav string 'ABOUT · HOME · BLOG · HELP · CONTACT → …', 'Pacific Northwest Made', 'Free to use (and modify) → $0 or £0 or ¥0 or €0', 'Mulțumesc! Support for 280+ łåŋģűąġéš', a paragraph of body text
instances.ux: Every line is contenteditable; mobile swaps in a separate set of single words per weight (Engineering, Association, Malagueñas…)
instances.learn: Write the sample lines as the font's own sales points (free, 280+ languages, bold for buttons): each line is specimen and pitch at once

reconstruction.layout: Section ~770px; label column right-aligned ending at x≈310; lines from x≈345, ~1050px wide; rows ~65px apart, body paragraph after a gap
reconstruction.typography: Labels ~10px caps grey #9aa; lines 24–48px in weights 300–900 of Figtree, dark teal #0d3b46; paragraph ~14px Regular, leading 1.5
reconstruction.behaviour: contenteditable lines; desktop and mobile containers swap via CSS
reconstruction.content: Self-promotional sample lines and a body paragraph

instances.look: On saturated yellow, the word 'tag!' as a thin outline (~450px) on faint metric lines, with four pointer callouts: 'Simple, monolinear construction', 'High x-height for maximum legibility', 'Friendly curved forms', 'Slight taper adds charm'; a small 'FIGTREE VERSION 1.000 LETTERFORM ANALYSIS' label top-left
instances.ux: The outline appears to draw itself in (stroke animation caught mid-way on the g)
instances.learn: A four-letter word drawn as outline with pin callouts sums up a sans in four claims

reconstruction.layout: Section ~1000px; SVG 785×430 viewBox centred (~1100px wide); callouts positioned by CSS vars --x/--y (%) with a vertical line and dot
reconstruction.typography: SVG <text> 'tag!' ~450px Figtree, fill none, 1px dark stroke; captions ~11px caps Figtree SemiBold, right- or left-aligned
reconstruction.behaviour: Outline stroke draw-on (stroke-dasharray/offset) when scrolled into view; pointers fade in

instances.look: A row of boxed controls (WEIGHT 500, SIZE 100, LETTER SPACE 0, LINE SPACE 110, ☑ CAPS) each with a slider below, over the editable headline 'Made with the finest in variable font technology' in navy; iridescent glass blobs float around it
instances.ux: Drag a slider or type a number in its box; Caps checkbox uppercases the text; blobs move at different speeds on scroll
instances.learn: Pair each slider with an editable number box: designers can set exact values instead of dragging

reconstruction.layout: Section ~1080px; control row from x≈230, 5 controls ~200px wide, 45px apart; sample text below at x≈230, ~900px wide; 4 blob PNGs absolutely placed at the edges
reconstruction.typography: Sample default 100px Figtree wght 500, line-height 110%, navy #12123a; control labels ~10px caps
reconstruction.behaviour: Range and number inputs sync both ways and set font-variation-settings wght 300–900, font-size 10–150px, letter-spacing −0.1–0.1em, line-height 60–150%; checkbox toggles text-transform; blobs have data-parallax data-speed −0.3…0.1

instances.look: On navy with a faint grid, four rows 'default → featured': FRACTIONS '1/2 3/5 8/13 → ½ ⅗ 8⁄13', MONOSPACE NUMBERS '$87.65 $12.34 $11.93' aligned, SCIENTIFIC INFERIORS 'C8H10N4O2 → C₈H₁₀N₄O₂', and 'ONE ALTERNATE "A" THAT JUST WANTS TO PARTY' 'ah yeah!'; a giant vertical 'features' word runs down the right edge
instances.ux: The right-hand column types itself out character by character when the row scrolls in; small (i) buttons show the CSS (font-feature-settings: 'frac') in a tooltip
instances.learn: Type the 'after' version live next to the static 'before', and give every feature an (i) tooltip with the exact CSS to copy

reconstruction.layout: Section ~1170px; rows at x≈230, before column ~480px, arrow ~80px, after column ~480px; rows ~240px apart; rotated heading 'features' ~120px Black at the right edge, reading top-to-bottom; background grid of 1px lines
reconstruction.typography: Samples ~48px Figtree Light white; labels ~10px caps grey with a grey 'i' chip; vertical heading ~120px wght 900 white
reconstruction.behaviour: IntersectionObserver triggers a typewriter fill of #fractions-after etc. with the feature applied (frac, tnum, sinf, ss01); tooltip on (i) hover shows data-tooltip
reconstruction.content: Feature names in plain English with jokey captions

instances.variantDefinition: Design notes written as running prose in which every letter mentioned is an inline clickable chip; clicking a chip loads that glyph large on its metric lines in a sticky side panel (often with a weight slider), so reading the rationale and inspecting the letter happen together.
instances.look: 'Design Notes' in Black, then a first-person essay whose mentioned glyphs (t, f, y, g, A, P, R, S, ?, !, comma, quotes, é, û, #, ‡, r, 1, 2, 5) are small pink rounded chips (the active one purple); to the right a sticky white panel 'LOWERCASE T' with a big t on Cap height / X height / Baseline / Descender lines and a WEIGHT 400 box with slider; fig-leaf photos frame the column
instances.ux: Click any chip → the panel shows that glyph and its name; the weight slider re-renders it from 300 to 900; on mobile the panel becomes an overlay with a close button
instances.learn: Turn every letter you write about into a button: the essay becomes the glyph browser

reconstruction.layout: Centred 980px container; text column ~520px left; inspector ~320px right, sticky, glyph box ~320×330 with 4 labelled horizontal metric lines, weight control below; decorative leaf PNGs at the right edge
reconstruction.typography: Heading ~60px Figtree Black; body ~16px Regular, leading 1.6, bold for key words; chips ~14px white on #e63fa0, radius 3px, active #5b2bd6; inspector glyph ~300px, metric labels ~9px caps grey
reconstruction.behaviour: a.letter-button click → sets .glyph-specimen text and .glyph-name from data-name, toggles .active; glyph-weight-slider/input set wght 300–900 on the specimen; panel position: sticky
reconstruction.content: Real designer's notes on t/f/y curves, widened caps, punctuation, numerals
reconstruction.assets: Leaf photo cut-outs (decorative), close icon SVG
reconstruction.html: p > a.letter-button[data-name='Lowercase T'] ; .glyph-inspector > h3.glyph-name + a.close-glyph-inspector + .glyph-box > p.glyph-specimen + span.glyph-cap-height/.glyph-x-height/.glyph-baseline/.glyph-descender + .glyph-weight-control > input#glyph-weight-input + input#glyph-weight-slider

instances.look: 'figtree' in Light ~80px, 'a friendly & free geometric sans', then two gradient buttons (blue→green): 'DOWNLOAD FROM GOOGLE FONTS →' and 'VIEW SOURCE ON GITHUB →'; a fig plant photo fills the right
instances.ux: Links out to Google Fonts and the GitHub repo; the fixed DOWNLOAD button anywhere on the page scrolls here
instances.learn: For an open-source font, offer both the consumer route (Google Fonts) and the source (GitHub) side by side
